issue_context.title: Support more collections in JSON source generator
issue_context.body:
The JSON source generator currently supports only `T[]`, `List<T>` (and derived types), and `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` (and derived types) collections. It should support all [collections supported](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json-supported-collection-types?pivots=dotnet-5-0) by existing `JsonSerializer` functionality.

This is more relevant now since we do not have a trim-safe way to support most collections (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/53205, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/52268, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/53256).

cc @eerhardt, @steveharter, @marek-safar, @jkotas

review_comments: Since this method call is only used to generate the expected JSON string, we don't really need to exercise any async APIs here.

Shouldn't this be
```suggestion
        public static JsonTypeInfo<TCollection> CreateImmutableDictionaryInfo<TCollection, TKey, TValue>(System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions options, System.Func<TCollection> createObjectFunc, JsonTypeInfo keyInfo, JsonTypeInfo valueInfo, System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonNumberHandling numberHandling, System.Action<Utf8JsonWriter, TCollection>? serializeFunc, System.Func<System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<System.Collections.Generic.KeyValuePair<TKey, TValue>>, TCollection> createRangeFunc) where TCollection : System.Collections.Immutable.IImmutableDictionary<TKey, TValue> where TKey : notnull { throw null; }
```
If not, how does this differ to the `CreateIReadOnlyDictionaryInfo` method?

We don't want STJ to take a direct dependency on System.Collections.Immutable.dll so that netstandard libraries using STJ aren't forced to take that dependency. Thus, we use reflection in the dynamic serializer implementation & source generated code-paths can reference accessors to those collections directly.

The difference from `CreateIReadOnlyDictionaryInfo` is that we are using the `ImmutableEnumerableConverter` in the implementation of this method, as opposed to the `IReadOnlyDictionary`-specific converter. Each collection converter has its own wrapping method so that we can trim out the unused ones.
Thanks for fixing this!

Am I right to assume that that we're resolving these type instances at runtime to facilitate potential trimming scenaria? If that's the case, doesn't the fact that we're introducing a static dependency to that type via the `typeof()` declarations in the RHS invalidate that benefit?

This (and every thing else in this assembly) is all compile-time inspection of types to figure out what code to generate, so the references made here don't cause things to be rooted in the trimmed app.
Got it. Why not just write something like `_stackType = typeof(Stack)` directly?

The Roslyn-compilation type system is complex. Basically the types in the generator-implementation dll are not the same as the types in the input compilation, so we have to resolve them each time the generator runs. cc @chsienki who might have a better answer.
What's an immutable IEnumerable and how does it differ from the `CreateEnumerableInfo` method?

Just needed a word to distinguish from Immutable dictionaries. `ImmutableEnumerable` sounded better than `ImmutableNonDictionary`, but we can get feedback in API review..

On the difference from `CreateEnumerableInfo`... same as https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/55566#discussion_r670677172.

does this account for the possibility that one converter instance is initialized by multiple `JsonTypeInfo` instances? I _think_ that it's occassionally possible although not sure it applies to converters that override `RequiresDynamicMemberAccessors`.

Hmm I think it could happen occasionally due to threading, but I think even in that case each `JsonTypeInfo` construction would create a separate converter instance, and the first one to complete would win, discarding the duplicates. Each converter instance would only be for a specific type, so there are no issues of creating invalid dynamic accessors.
I assume the code here is a simple move, no changes?
Correct - no changes.
This is dangerous. We now have a ctor that isn't marked with RUC, so this justifciation no longer holds.
Would adding a separate, reflection-free converter for source-gen usage be a better approach? Luckily we have just 3 converter types that use this pattern, so it wouldn't be a lot of duplication.

I think that might be a good idea. I'm a little nervous that while today we don't have an issue here, someone could edit the code later and start calling these methods in different combinations and we wouldn't get warnings because of these invalid suppressions.
I opened https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/55846.
Assert `builderName != null` here and below?
nit: could use StringBuilder ctor that takes `type.FullName` (here and other similar)
I'll make a dedicated PR addressing this.
Only works when < 10 generic values? (which is fine for known types, but not things like `Func<,,,,,,,,,,>`)
This is related to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/55566#discussion_r670101418. I think we can remove this manual code altogether; will tackle in follow up.
I believe this method and others here are not used directly by STJ.dll -- only the source-gen assembly. Ideally these are moved to a source-gen only file to save a bit of assembly size.

It is used by STJ.dll as well. It used to be inlined within `GetImmutableDictionaryConstructingType`, but I needed this specific function in the generator as well. I'll leave as-is in this PR, but I think we can refactor and remove the use of `bool sourceGenType = false` in a follow-up.
FWIW the `System.Text.Json.Tests.Serialization` namespace has crept up in quite a few other places as well.
Ditto for this and all the other `expectedJson` values in this file.
I assume these tests were just moved...
Yup, simply moved to share them with the source generator tests.
